slots_and_copies.name: slot_0
slots_and_copies.selection_rule: Only one save region exists; FUN_0801d55c unconditionally reads all 64 blocks (0x00-0x3F) with no slot-select read beforehand. No second magic-tagged region or backup copy was found anywhere in the 512-byte file.

checksums.name: candidate_subtract_accumulate
checksums.formula_detail: 16-bit running subtraction accumulator over 254 (0xfe) bytes starting at the record base: uVar6=0; for i in 0..0xfd: uVar6 = (uVar6 - byte[i]) & 0xffff; final uVar6 stored as a 16-bit value at offset base+0xfe. Found in FUN_0801d384, but could NOT be matched against either real .sav file at any tried base offset (0x00 or 0x04) or endianness, and the candidate target bytes (file 0xFE/0xFF or 0x102/0x103) fall in the all-zero unused tail of the file, suggesting this loop applies to a non-persisted scratch structure rather than the on-disk 512-byte image.

io_driver_functions.notes: Generic DMA3 bit-serial clock-N-bits primitive used by every EEPROM operation; programs DMA3 control and busy-waits on a status bit.
EEPROM read of one 8-byte (4x u16) block: serializes a READ opcode + 6-bit block address, then clocks back 68 bits and unpacks 4 u16 words.
EEPROM write of one 8-byte (4x u16) block: serializes WRITE opcode + block address + 64 data bits + stop bit; guards with FUN_08032680/FUN_08032708 IRQ mask toggles and polls the EEPROM busy bit.
Not a stored checksum - a post-write read-back VERIFY: reads a block via FUN_080327cc and compares all 4 u16 words against the expected value, returning 0x8000 on mismatch, 0 on match.
IRQ/DMA critical-section enter, used only around the EEPROM write command.

open_questions: What does the 254-byte subtract-accumulate loop in FUN_0801d384 actually checksum, if anything persisted? It did not match either real .sav file at any offset/endianness tried.

Is the ±1-byte offset ambiguity between the hardcoded 0x16 write (decompiled offset param_1+0x1b) and the real constant byte at file offset 0x1C a genuine decompiler artifact, or evidence of an additional 1-byte field we have not identified?

What is the true semantic meaning of the 12-byte nibble-packed block at 0x08-0x13 and the mutating word at 0xF8-0xF9? Only structural/positional evidence exists; no gameplay-linked .ss save states were available in this packet to correlate.

Why does ghidra/callgraph.json report empty caller lists for FUN_0801d55c, FUN_0801d698, FUN_0803287c, and FUN_08032958 despite real call sites existing in ghidra/decompiled.c? (Likely because all are reached only via unresolved indirect/jump-table calls that Ghidra could not statically link.)

Does a failed EEPROM write (FUN_0803287c returning non-zero) during FUN_0801d2ec's flush loop actually skip the read-back verify pass, as the decompiled OR-accumulated return code suggests, and what are the real-world reliability implications?
